ai.description: This 4–6 cm frog is green above with white-spotted flanks. It features bright red webbing between its toes and a distinct white line along the upper lip and outer limbs. Family: Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Rhacophorus rhodopus* is best distinguished by its vibrant, bright red webbing between the fingers and toes, which contrasts sharply with the pale or translucent feet of similar species.
ai.habitat: The Red-webbed Treefrog inhabits subtropical evergreen and moist deciduous forests, typically found in vegetation near streams at altitudes between 200 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The red-webbed treefrog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights hunting for insects among the foliage of tropical forests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhacophorus rhodopus* breeds during the monsoon, laying foam nests on leaves overhanging water. Each clutch contains approximately 100–200 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Rhacophorus rhodopus* is found in Northeast India, primarily in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, inhabiting tropical forests at elevations between 200 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Red-webbed Treefrog emits a series of rapid, high-pitched "chirp" pulses, typically heard from vegetation surrounding forest pools and streams.
